09.2.old: Seats "close enforcer" and "judge contradiction enforcer". Alternate Merge adds the rows to enforcer_log.
09.2.new:
Seats "close enforcer" and "judge contradiction enforcer". Alternate Merge adds the rows to enforcer_log.
    - ONE CLOSING CHECK: THE CLOSING ENFORCER ALSO READS THE REVERSED READINGS (ASK 590 and ASK 595; ruling 427; Close Enforcer Build, Close Enforcer Record, Panel Build, Build Independent Verdict, Close Group Batch Build, Send Back Build, Alt Send Back Build, the child's R2 Alt Send Back Build, and the Shared Library, both copies; where it differs from any anti-cheat entry of this manual, this entry is right):
      - The anti-cheat path is out of the flow. Close Enforcer Build leads to Assume Check Build; Check Save and Regrade After Quotes? (true) lead to Panel Build. The six Anticheat nodes stay in the workflow, reached by nothing, and the close group batch carries no anti-cheat items. Panel Build and Build Independent Verdict still hold the [ANTI-CHEAT CHECK] note text in `__ACX`; it writes nothing, because it returns empty unless Anticheat Record ran, and nothing reaches Anticheat Record.
      - VERSE candidates: Close Enforcer Build adds to each side's two reads the candidates X1, X2, ..., found by the anti-cheat finder: one verse that the side reads in its close ([CR4] or [DR4]) and in its rounds 1 to 3, with both texts. A block is not the side's reading when it quotes six or more words that stand in the other side's rounds outside quotation marks; a verse both sides quote does not count as the other side's words. At most 120,000 characters of VERSE items a side; any rest is listed as rev_not_checked.
      - The enforcer answers each VERSE candidate CONFIRMED, REVERSED READING or NOT A CONTRADICTION. A reading is reversed in two ways: the close draws from the verse a conclusion the side's earlier words deny, or denies a conclusion they drew; or the close asserts again a claim about the verse that the same side earlier withdrew, dropped or gave up. Not a reversal: the close repeats, narrows, adds footing, answers the opponent or keeps the earlier reading; a fuller quotation or gloss of the same word; a close that itself withdraws or grants an earlier claim; earlier words that name the verse and state no reading of it.
      - Close Enforcer Record lets a REVERSED READING stand only when all hold: the id is a VERSE candidate of that side; the earlier round is that side's round 1 to 3 and the closing round its round 4; both quotations stand word for word in those rounds; neither quotation stands under another verse than the candidate's (pkgOVS, the governing-verse check); the earlier quotation is not the other side's own words standing in its rounds outside quotation marks ("NOT REVERSED (other side's words)"); and the other independent read gives the same id REVERSED READING or CONFIRMED ("NOT REVERSED (one check of two)" otherwise). A CONFIRMED contradiction of the same candidate, or of the same side and closing sentence, stands in its place ("REVERSED (CONFIRMED stands)"). The list is kept once per side and verse (cec.reversed).
      - The judges' block (Panel Build), under the [CONFIRMED CLOSING CONTRADICTIONS ...] block of each close round, in place of the [ANTI-CHEAT CHECK] notes: "[REVERSED CLOSE SENTENCES -- found by the system's closing enforcer in two independent reads and checked by code, not by a judge (ruling 427: a close round that reverses the same side's own earlier reading of a verse)." then, for each, "- <SIDE> on <verse>: the closing round [<round>] says: "...". The same side said in [<round>]: "...". The close sentence is disregarded (this by itself breaks no link; only a pair listed under CONFIRMED CLOSING CONTRADICTIONS is confirmed); grade this side's earlier answer on <verse> on its own words, against the verse." and last "A judge that holds a listed sentence is not reversed says so with its reason; the judge keeps the decision (ruling 428).]" Each quoted sentence is shown whole.
      - The send-back (E-REVCLOSE; Send Back Build, Alt Send Back Build, R2 Alt Send Back Build): a judge line that quotes 8 or more words in a row of a reversed close sentence goes back once, one item per judge per side and verse, with both quotations and both rounds (each quoted sentence whole), ending "KEEP your line with your reason, or CHANGE it. Either answer is accepted and recorded; the judge keeps the decision (ruling 428); this item counts against no seat." Not sent back: a line that says REVERSED, disregard or NOT HELD; IMPOSED, ANSWER CHECK, CONTRADICTION(S), CITATION CHECK and WITHDRAWAL CHECK lines; AUDIT and EXTRACTOR lines. The code does not decide whether the line rests on the sentence; the judge answers that with KEEP and its reason.
      - The item is record-only in all three send-back records: KEEP or CHANGE makes the row CURED, and a CHANGE is applied like any send-back answer; no answer, or a reply error, is recorded and counted nowhere. The item enters no count list.
      - The judge's line in the item is whole (ASK 595): the item's flagged_line and response_line hold the judge's line uncut, whatever its length.
      - Size: each enforcer read grows from 55,000 to 98,000 characters up to 142,000 to 190,000 characters on the four stored runs measured; no new call.
      - Limits: the finder is the anti-cheat finder unchanged, so a reading line under an ANSWER heading that does not name the verse itself is not tied to that verse. No REVERSED READING answer by the enforcer model is stored from any run, so the offline proofs planted the answer; how many a live read gives is not known. Not shown by a run.

09.1.new:
- E-HOLD through the gate (ECW HOLD on): an E-HOLD DISAGREE that pushes a line toward UNDERDETERMINED passes the same CARRIED BY gate as E-COL, DeepSeek's E-HOLD rule asks for CARRIED BY, and the send-back shows the judge the row.
  - A DISAGREE ANSWERS EVERY VERSE ON THE JUDGE'S GROUND (ASK 586 J6; Shared Library, both copies: the E-COL and E-HOLD instructions, the reply parser read by the three Judge Enforcer Record nodes, and module ECW `gateJ6`):
    - Why: in run 42071 the enforcer told a judge its break on D2 vs C6 was wrong, citing one verse (Luke 1:33), while the judge's GROUND rested on Jeremiah 22:30 and Acts 2:30, which the enforcer did not answer; that item began the seat's removal.
    - Instruction: the E-COL text, after "Read the answer with every other verse either side quoted on the subject (Isaiah 28:10).", reads "A DISAGREE answers every verse on the judge's GROUND line: for each one, a clause that quotes it and says why it does not carry the judge's grade, or one CARRIED BY for each. A DISAGREE that leaves a verse of the GROUND unanswered is recorded and not sent back." The E-HOLD text, after "Without it the push is recorded and not sent back.", reads the same with "says why it leaves the point open".
    - Code: the reply parser keeps, for each "ENFORCER: <id>" line, the lines that follow it up to the next ENFORCER line, whole. When the gate would send a DISAGREE, `gateJ6` also requires: every CARRIED BY on the reply line passes the gate, not only the last; and every verse reference on the judge's GROUND (from "GROUND:" to the next field, read from the judge's whole line) is cited in the item, on the reply line or in the lines kept with it. An "ENGAGE ... -- NO" line names verses without answering them and is not an answer. A range on the GROUND is answered only by a citation that covers the whole range.
    - A miss is held, not sent: the row reads "ENFORCER HELD (pkgECW, recorded, not sent back: RECORDED, NOT SENT BACK, ASK 586 J6: the enforcer's DISAGREE does not answer <references>, on the judge's GROUND)". It touches no seat and no count, and the judge's grade stands (ruling 428). The pressed-verse rule (ASK 355) is unchanged and runs on each CARRIED BY.
    - Limits: a citation counts as an answer; the code does not read whether the clause says why the verse does not carry the grade. A right correction by the enforcer that leaves one GROUND verse uncited does not reach the judge. Shown offline on stored row 53043 of run 42071 (sent before, held after, naming Jeremiah 22:30 and Acts 2:30). Not shown by a run.

08.0.old: BROKEN gives CHALLENGER WINS when CHALLENGE STANDING is SELF-SUPPORTED and no collision on that seat is graded CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN (ASK 517), and UNDERDETERMINED otherwise;
08.0.new: BROKEN gives CHALLENGER WINS when CHALLENGE STANDING is SELF-SUPPORTED, no collision on that seat is graded CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN (ASK 517) and the seat's KEYSTONE line does not read STANDS (ASK 586 J1), and UNDERDETERMINED otherwise;

08.0.old: The seat's word is given by the engine from these rules, not taken from the judge's RESULT line (ONE DECIDER FOR THE RESULT WORD, below).
08.0.new:
The seat's word is given by the engine from these rules, not taken from the judge's RESULT line (ONE DECIDER FOR THE RESULT WORD, below).
- A RESULT AGAINST THE DEFENDER NEEDS THE KEYSTONE BROKEN (ASK 586 J1; Panel Build, Build Independent Verdict, and the Shared Library, both copies; it holds whichever side the Oracle sits on):
  - Judges' text, after "BROKEN gives CHALLENGER WINS when CHALLENGE STANDING is SELF-SUPPORTED, and UNDERDETERMINED when it is PROP-DEPENDENT or COLLAPSED.": "A RESULT against the defender requires your KEYSTONE line to read BROKEN, by a collision line on the keystone link or by the link it rests on. If your keystone line reads STANDS, you may not write a RESULT against the defender: write UNDERDETERMINED unless your verdict is HELD."
  - The seat's word: where the rules above give CHALLENGER WINS and the seat's KEYSTONE line reads STANDS, the word is UNDERDETERMINED. The break stays on its collision line and counts as a broken link; it does not carry the conclusion. The engine applies this in the three places it computes the word (the recompute, the audit tag and the gate after the send-back), and the record then names the rule: "KEYSTONE STANDS (the keystone link is not broken; ASK 586 J1 ...)". Any word but STANDS, or a KEYSTONE line the reader cannot read, moves no word.
  - The reader (`ks586`) reads the word STANDS, BROKEN, WITHDRAWN or UNDERDETERMINED after "--", an em dash, an en dash, a dash or a colon, in "KEYSTONE: D<n> -- STANDS" and in the form "KEYSTONE: D<n> vs C<m> (<references>) -- STANDS".
  - Shown offline, nothing stored rewritten: with the Oracle as challenger (171 runs, 513 judgments, 2026-10-02 to 11-17), 149 judgments read CHALLENGER WINS, and 56 of them, in 32 runs, stand beside KEYSTONE STANDS and would read UNDERDETERMINED. With the Oracle as defender (runs 41418, 41822, 42071), 3 of 9 judgments (1271, 1272, 1273). Not shown by a run.
